verses.text: King Ahasuerus laid a tribute on the land, and on the islands of the sea.

All the acts of his power and of his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king advanced him, aren’t they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
For Mordecai the Jew was next to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted by the multitude of his brothers, seeking the good of his people, and speaking peace to all his descendants.

footnotes.content: A king's power measured in tributes and taxes—how quickly the world counts greatness. But here we glimpse what was never written in those chronicles: a hidden hand at work, a remnant preserved, a Jewish girl who became queen and saved her people. Mordecai and Esther knew the King of kings had written them into history.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Written in the book of the chronicles"—the official record honors Mordecai's advancement, yet it remains silent about the real story behind it. How often does the world's history miss the deepest truth? What matters is that the Lord saw, and Mordecai walked in the light of that seeing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in Mordecai's life: a man faithful in his corner, seeking the good of his people, speaking peace—and the Lord raises him high. We live in a time when quiet faithfulness can feel overlooked, yet history shows us again and again that the Lord sees the faithful few and exalts them in His time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
